The manager may favour its own interest.
mocks.w: Correct: The manager must act in the client's best interest, with care, diligence and loyalty, and place client interest before its own.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Sector concentration” is correct?
o: Growth investors buy only stocks with the lowest P/E.
Quality investing seeks the most indebted firms.
Concentrating a portfolio in one sector raises risk because sector-specific shocks hit all holdings together.
Sector concentration lowers portfolio risk.
mocks.w: Correct: Concentrating a portfolio in one sector raises risk because sector-specific shocks hit all holdings together.

mocks.p: A manager chooses strong businesses one by one. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Bottom-up approach
Investment objective
Behavioural biases
Concentrated portfolio
mocks.w: This is Bottom-up approach. The bottom-up approach starts with analysing individual companies, regardless of macro or sector views.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Inflation” is correct?
o: Inflation raises the real return of cash.
Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money; real return is nominal return minus inflation, approximately.
Equity and debt are the same asset class.
The time value of money is the interest on a loan.
mocks.w: Correct: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money; real return is nominal return minus inflation, approximately.

mocks.p: Shares bought today are delivered the next working day. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Settlement
SEBI
Secondary market
Stock exchange
mocks.w: This is Settlement. Equity trades settle on T+1 through a clearing corporation, which guarantees settlement.

mocks.p: A long bond falls more than a short one when rates rise. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Coupon and yield
Duration
Credit risk
Credit rating
mocks.w: This is Duration. Duration measures a bond's price sensitivity to interest-rate changes; higher duration means larger price swings.

mocks.p: The client acts on the manager's recommendation herself. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Investment approach
Advisory PMS
Segregation of client assets
Investor charter
mocks.w: This is Advisory PMS. In advisory PMS the manager only advises; the client decides and executes.

mocks.p: Which statement about “PMS versus mutual fund” is correct?
o: NAV is used to value a PMS client's individual holdings.
In PMS, securities are held in the client's own account and each trade is tax-relevant for the client; in mutual funds, investors hold pooled units.
PMS clients cannot see holdings.
In PMS, assets are pooled with other clients' money.
mocks.w: Correct: In PMS, securities are held in the client's own account and each trade is tax-relevant for the client; in mutual funds, investors hold pooled units.

mocks.p: A distributor completes certification before selling PMS. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Distributor registration
Net worth requirement
Penalties
Prohibition on assured returns
mocks.w: This is Distributor registration. Distributors of PMS must hold the NISM XXI-A certificate and an AMFI ARN, and follow code of conduct.

mocks.p: Each client's holdings are separate in a PMS account. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Discretionary PMS
Non-discretionary PMS
Limits on pooling
Portfolio manager
mocks.w: This is Limits on pooling. A portfolio manager cannot pool client funds the way a mutual fund does; each client's portfolio is managed individually.

mocks.p: An investor looks at returns after costs. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Gross versus net returns
Benchmark
Risk-adjusted evaluation
Standardised reporting
mocks.w: This is Gross versus net returns. Gross returns are before fees and expenses while net returns are after them; investors should compare net returns.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Risk-adjusted evaluation” is correct?
o: Evaluating a manager involves return, risk, consistency, process and costs, not just headline returns.
Any index can serve as the benchmark.
The Sharpe ratio considers only returns.
Only the last year's return matters.
mocks.w: Correct: Evaluating a manager involves return, risk, consistency, process and costs, not just headline returns.

mocks.p: A document sets limits on equity and single-stock exposure. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Constraints
Tactical asset allocation
Investment policy
Rebalancing
mocks.w: This is Investment policy. The investment policy records objectives, constraints, allocation ranges and rebalancing rules, guiding the manager.

mocks.p: A loss on one sale offsets a gain on another. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Short-term and long-term gains
Set-off of losses
Turnover and tax
Taxation at client level
mocks.w: This is Set-off of losses. Capital losses can be set off against capital gains and carried forward as per the tax law.

mocks.p: A concentrated portfolio suffers when its top holding falls. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Asset class
Investment horizon
Risk types
Compounding
mocks.w: This is Risk types. Investment risks include market, credit, liquidity, interest-rate and concentration risks.

mocks.p: Which statement about “ETF” is correct?
o: In PMS, assets are pooled with other clients' money.
A mutual fund holds each investor's securities separately.
An ETF is bought only from the AMC at NAV.
An ETF is a fund traded on exchanges, typically tracking an index at low cost.
mocks.w: Correct: An ETF is a fund traded on exchanges, typically tracking an index at low cost.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Equity risks” is correct?
o: Equity cannot lose capital over short periods.
Governance does not affect investment risk.
P/B compares price with dividend.
Equity investors face market, company-specific, valuation and liquidity risks, and can lose capital.
mocks.w: Correct: Equity investors face market, company-specific, valuation and liquidity risks, and can lose capital.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Disclosure document” is correct?
o: Costs are not passed to PMS clients.
The disclosure document gives the client full information about the manager, investment approach, fees, risks and litigation before signing.
A high-water mark resets every month.
The disclosure document is given after the first year.
mocks.w: Correct: The disclosure document gives the client full information about the manager, investment approach, fees, risks and litigation before signing.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Hedging uses derivatives to offset an existing risk, reducing the portfolio's exposure to adverse moves.
o: Options
Hedging
Derivative
Futures
mocks.w: Hedging: Hedging uses derivatives to offset an existing risk, reducing the portfolio's exposure to adverse moves.

mocks.p: A client who exits early pays a decreasing charge. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Hybrid fee
Client reporting
Termination
Exit load
mocks.w: This is Exit load. Exit load is a charge on withdrawal in the early years: at most 3% in the first year, 2% in the second and 1% in the third, with none thereafter.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The primary market is where securities are first issued to investors and the issuer receives the proceeds.
o: Depository
Primary market
SEBI
Stock exchange
mocks.w: Primary market: The primary market is where securities are first issued to investors and the issuer receives the proceeds.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Stock exchange” is correct?
o: A stock exchange issues shares to the public.
A depository sets stock prices.
The company receives funds from secondary market trades.
A stock exchange is a regulated platform where listed securities trade, such as the BSE and NSE.
mocks.w: Correct: A stock exchange is a regulated platform where listed securities trade, such as the BSE and NSE.

mocks.p: A client wants long-term growth with moderate risk. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Behavioural biases
Constraints
Investment objective
Portfolio turnover
mocks.w: This is Investment objective. The investment objective states what the portfolio is meant to achieve, such as growth, income or capital preservation, with risk and time limits.

mocks.p: A client considers the tax treatment of fees paid. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Capital gains statement
Set-off of losses
Turnover and tax
Tax on fees
mocks.w: This is Tax on fees. Management fees and expenses may be deductible against gains or income as per the law, subject to conditions.

mocks.p: A manager discloses its group company's shares in a client's portfolio. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Penalties
Distributor registration
Related-party dealing
SEBI Portfolio Managers Regulations
mocks.w: This is Related-party dealing. Managers must disclose investments in related-party securities and avoid favouring group entities.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Commission disclosure” is correct?
o: Distributors must disclose commission earned from the portfolio manager to the client.
Distributors may guarantee returns.
Commissions are hidden from clients.
Portfolio managers are free from regulation.
mocks.w: Correct: Distributors must disclose commission earned from the portfolio manager to the client.

mocks.p: A small price move leads to a large loss on margin. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Options
Leverage risk
Derivative
Futures
mocks.w: This is Leverage risk. Derivatives allow large exposure for small margin, magnifying gains and losses.

mocks.p: A client transfers existing shares to start a PMS. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Contribution of securities
Termination
Withdrawals and partial redemptions
High-water mark
mocks.w: This is Contribution of securities. Clients may contribute securities instead of cash, and the manager may hold them or realign the portfolio, with tax consequences.

mocks.p: A manager keeps 8% in cash for opportunities. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Strategic asset allocation
Review and monitoring
Tax-aware management
Cash in the portfolio
mocks.w: This is Cash in the portfolio. Holding cash gives liquidity and flexibility but can drag returns in rising markets.

mocks.p: A manager sells a position when it falls to a pre-set level. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Top-down approach
Passive management
Stop-loss and risk limits
Strategic asset allocation
mocks.w: This is Stop-loss and risk limits. Risk limits such as stop-losses, single-stock caps and sector caps control downside and discipline.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Growth investing” is correct?
o: Growth investors buy only stocks with the lowest P/E.
Governance does not affect investment risk.
Small caps are less volatile than large caps.
Growth investing seeks companies with above-average earnings growth, often at higher valuations.
mocks.w: Correct: Growth investing seeks companies with above-average earnings growth, often at higher valuations.

mocks.p: A client receives a quarterly report on holdings and returns. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Exit load
Hurdle rate
Conflict of interest
Client reporting
mocks.w: This is Client reporting. Managers must give clients periodic reports showing portfolio holdings, transactions, performance and charges.

mocks.p: A bond rated BBB is more exposed than one rated AAA. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Money market instruments
Coupon and yield
Bond
Credit risk
mocks.w: This is Credit risk. Credit risk is the possibility that the issuer fails to pay interest or principal on time.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? A concentrated portfolio holds few stocks, offering higher potential returns with higher risk.
o: Concentrated portfolio
Top-down approach
Active management
Bottom-up approach
mocks.w: Concentrated portfolio: A concentrated portfolio holds few stocks, offering higher potential returns with higher risk.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Corporate governance” is correct?
o: P/B compares price with dividend.
Governance does not affect investment risk.
Good governance, with independent boards and transparent disclosure, reduces the risk of value loss to minority shareholders.
Equity cannot lose capital over short periods.
mocks.w: Correct: Good governance, with independent boards and transparent disclosure, reduces the risk of value loss to minority shareholders.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Large, mid and small caps” is correct?
o: Small caps are less volatile than large caps.
Large caps are generally more stable and liquid; small caps offer higher growth potential with more volatility and lower liquidity.
Sector concentration lowers portfolio risk.
Growth investors buy only stocks with the lowest P/E.
mocks.w: Correct: Large caps are generally more stable and liquid; small caps offer higher growth potential with more volatility and lower liquidity.

mocks.p: A distributor checks a client's risk profile and net worth before recommending PMS. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Suitability by distributor
Prohibition on assured returns
SEBI Portfolio Managers Regulations
Conflict of interest
mocks.w: This is Suitability by distributor. The distributor must assess the client's suitability, explain risks and fees and give the disclosure document before onboarding.

mocks.p: A manager limits any single stock to 10% of the portfolio. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Stop-loss and risk limits
Tax-aware management
Position sizing
Tactical asset allocation
mocks.w: This is Position sizing. Position sizing sets how much of the portfolio is placed in each security, balancing conviction and risk.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Passive management” is correct?
o: Passive management replicates an index at low cost, without attempting to outperform.
Tax does not affect PMS decisions.
Active managers track the index exactly.
Passive managers pick stocks they expect to beat the market.
mocks.w: Correct: Passive management replicates an index at low cost, without attempting to outperform.

mocks.p: A portfolio holding 25 stocks across sectors. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Compounding
Inflation
Time value of money
Diversification
mocks.w: This is Diversification. Diversification spreads investments across securities and asset classes to reduce specific risk.

mocks.p: The manager earns a fee only when returns exceed 8%. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Exit load
Hurdle rate
Hybrid fee
Custodian
mocks.w: This is Hurdle rate. A hurdle rate is the minimum return the portfolio must earn before a performance fee is charged.

mocks.p: A manager picks sectors first and then stocks. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Position sizing
Top-down approach
Tactical asset allocation
Strategic asset allocation
mocks.w: This is Top-down approach. The top-down approach starts with economy and sector views and then selects stocks within favoured sectors.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Return on equity” is correct?
o: Sector concentration lowers portfolio risk.
ROE is net profit divided by shareholders' equity and measures how effectively equity is used.
Equity gives a fixed return.
ROE is price divided by earnings.
mocks.w: Correct: ROE is net profit divided by shareholders' equity and measures how effectively equity is used.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Investment approach” is correct?
o: Clients can invest in PMS only through distributors.
PMS accepts investments of ₹5 lakh from retail clients.
An investment approach is a distinct style or strategy offered by a portfolio manager, such as large-cap growth or multi-cap value, with defined objectives and risks.
An investment approach is a promise of returns.
mocks.w: Correct: An investment approach is a distinct style or strategy offered by a portfolio manager, such as large-cap growth or multi-cap value, with defined objectives and risks.

mocks.p: A scheme's value per unit is ₹40. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Alternative investment fund
NAV
Mutual fund
ETF
mocks.w: This is NAV. NAV is the per-unit value of a scheme, equal to net assets divided by units outstanding.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Money market instruments” is correct?
o: Duration is the bond's maturity date.
Money market instruments mature within a year and are used to park short-term funds.
Money market instruments mature in 10 years.
A bond gives ownership in the company.
mocks.w: Correct: Money market instruments mature within a year and are used to park short-term funds.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Audit and compliance” is correct?
o: Portfolio managers are never audited.
A return-based fee is charged even if the portfolio loses money.
A PMS can start without a written agreement.
Portfolio managers are subject to annual audits and reporting to SEBI, and must have compliance officers.
mocks.w: Correct: Portfolio managers are subject to annual audits and reporting to SEBI, and must have compliance officers.

mocks.p: A manager's activities are bound by SEBI's rules. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Insider trading
Code of conduct for distributors
SEBI Portfolio Managers Regulations
Conflict of interest
mocks.w: This is SEBI Portfolio Managers Regulations. These regulations govern registration, conduct, fees, disclosures and client protection for portfolio managers.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Non-discretionary PMS” is correct?
o: In non-discretionary PMS the manager advises and executes only after the client's prior approval for each decision.
The manager decides without consulting the client.
A manager may hold client assets alongside its own.
PMS accepts investments of ₹5 lakh from retail clients.
mocks.w: Correct: In non-discretionary PMS the manager advises and executes only after the client's prior approval for each decision.

mocks.p: An independent institution holds client assets. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Contribution of securities
Hurdle rate
Custodian
High-water mark
mocks.w: This is Custodian. A custodian safekeeps the securities of PMS clients independent of the manager, and settles trades.

mocks.p: A contract based on the Nifty 50. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Options
Derivative
Leverage risk
Hedging
mocks.w: This is Derivative. A derivative is a contract whose value depends on an underlying asset, such as a share or an index.

mocks.p: A bank at ₹300 with book value of ₹150 trades at 2 times. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Equity share
Market capitalisation
Corporate governance
Price-to-book ratio
mocks.w: This is Price-to-book ratio. P/B compares share price with book value per share, widely used for banks and asset-heavy companies.

mocks.p: A manager tries to beat the index through stock selection. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Active management
Portfolio turnover
Behavioural biases
Investment policy
mocks.w: This is Active management. Active management seeks to outperform a benchmark through selection and timing decisions, at higher cost.

mocks.p: A client adds dividend credited to her account to income. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Set-off of losses
Tax on fees
Dividend income
Short-term and long-term gains
mocks.w: This is Dividend income. Dividend received on shares in the portfolio is taxable in the client's hands at the slab rate.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Distributors must act honestly, avoid mis-selling, keep confidentiality and give true information about products.
o: Code of conduct for distributors
Conflict of interest
Related-party dealing
Fiduciary duty
mocks.w: Code of conduct for distributors: Distributors must act honestly, avoid mis-selling, keep confidentiality and give true information about products.

mocks.p: A firm with insufficient net worth cannot be registered. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Investment approach
Direct onboarding
Segregation of client assets
Registration of portfolio managers
mocks.w: This is Registration of portfolio managers. Portfolio managers must be registered with SEBI and meet net-worth requirements; the minimum net worth is ₹5 crore.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Portfolio turnover” is correct?
o: Turnover has no effect on costs.
A bottom-up approach begins with the macro view.
Passive managers pick stocks they expect to beat the market.
Portfolio turnover measures how much of the portfolio is bought and sold in a year; high turnover raises costs and taxes.
mocks.w: Correct: Portfolio turnover measures how much of the portfolio is bought and sold in a year; high turnover raises costs and taxes.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Quality investing” is correct?
o: Small caps are less volatile than large caps.
Growth investors buy only stocks with the lowest P/E.
Quality investing favours companies with high returns on capital, stable earnings and strong governance.
Quality investing seeks the most indebted firms.
mocks.w: Correct: Quality investing favours companies with high returns on capital, stable earnings and strong governance.

mocks.p: A manager who trades frequently generates more short-term gains. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Turnover and tax
Short-term and long-term gains
Capital gains statement
Set-off of losses
mocks.w: This is Turnover and tax. High portfolio turnover can push more gains into short-term, increasing the tax cost.

mocks.p: A manager buys and sells for the client based on the strategy without consent. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Registration of portfolio managers
Investment approach
Segregation of client assets
Discretionary PMS
mocks.w: This is Discretionary PMS. In discretionary PMS the manager takes investment decisions independently on behalf of the client, without asking approval for each trade.

mocks.p: A PMS client is billed management fee and performance fee. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mutual fund
Alternative investment fund
PMS versus mutual fund
Expense versus fee
mocks.w: This is Expense versus fee. Mutual funds charge an expense ratio inside NAV, while PMS charges management and performance fees separately to the client.

mocks.p: A large-cap approach quietly buys small caps. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Standard deviation
Up and down capture
Money-weighted return
Style drift
mocks.w: This is Style drift. Style drift occurs when a manager moves away from the stated investment approach, which should be monitored.

mocks.p: Reinvested gains themselves earn further gains. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Asset class
Risk types
Compounding
Diversification
mocks.w: This is Compounding. Compounding generates returns on past returns, growing wealth faster over long horizons.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Sharpe ratio” is correct?
o: The Sharpe ratio measures excess return per unit of total risk; a higher ratio means better risk-adjusted performance.
The Sharpe ratio considers only returns.
Gross returns are what the client receives.
TWRR is affected by when the client adds money.
mocks.w: Correct: The Sharpe ratio measures excess return per unit of total risk; a higher ratio means better risk-adjusted performance.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? An AIF is a privately pooled vehicle for sophisticated investors with a minimum of ₹1 crore.
o: Alternative investment fund
NAV
Transparency
Expense versus fee
mocks.w: Alternative investment fund: An AIF is a privately pooled vehicle for sophisticated investors with a minimum of ₹1 crore.

mocks.p: A manager charges 2% of assets every year. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Return-based fee
Withdrawals and partial redemptions
Hurdle rate
Fixed fee
mocks.w: This is Fixed fee. A fixed management fee is charged as a percentage of assets irrespective of performance.

mocks.p: A portfolio captures 110% of rising markets and 80% of falling markets. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Money-weighted return
Consistency
Style drift
Up and down capture
mocks.w: This is Up and down capture. Capture ratios show how much of the benchmark's up and down moves a portfolio captures; high up-capture and low down-capture is desirable.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Risk types” is correct?
o: Risk profile is irrelevant to PMS.
Investment risks include market, credit, liquidity, interest-rate and concentration risks.
Diversification removes all risk.
Concentration risk applies only to bonds.
mocks.w: Correct: Investment risks include market, credit, liquidity, interest-rate and concentration risks.

mocks.p: A manager sticks to the process despite market noise. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Behavioural biases
Active management
Investment objective
Constraints
mocks.w: This is Behavioural biases. Biases like overconfidence, herding and loss aversion lead to poor decisions; a disciplined process counters them.

mocks.p: A manager picks businesses with durable returns and low debt. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Value investing
Quality investing
Large, mid and small caps
Equity risks
mocks.w: This is Quality investing. Quality investing favours companies with high returns on capital, stable earnings and strong governance.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Partial withdrawals are never allowed.
A custodian safekeeps the securities of PMS clients independent of the manager, and settles trades.
A hurdle rate is the minimum return the portfolio must earn before a performance fee is charged.
Managers must give clients periodic reports showing portfolio holdings, transactions, performance and charges.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Clients may withdraw funds or securities as per the agreement, with notice and exit load as applicable.

mocks.p: A high-net-worth client with a ten-year horizon is a candidate. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Bottom-up approach
Tactical asset allocation
Investment policy
Suitability for PMS
mocks.w: This is Suitability for PMS. PMS suits investors with large surplus funds, long horizons and ability to bear volatility and concentration risk.

mocks.p: A client who needs cash in two years cannot hold illiquid assets. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Constraints
Passive management
Behavioural biases
Stop-loss and risk limits
mocks.w: This is Constraints. Constraints such as liquidity needs, time horizon, tax, legal limits and unique preferences shape what the portfolio can hold.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Turnover and tax” is correct?
o: Losses can never be set off.
The holding period for listed shares is 36 months.
Turnover has no tax effect.
High portfolio turnover can push more gains into short-term, increasing the tax cost.
mocks.w: Correct: High portfolio turnover can push more gains into short-term, increasing the tax cost.

mocks.p: The manager earns a share only of returns above 10%. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Hybrid fee
Brokerage and expenses
Fixed fee
Return-based fee
mocks.w: This is Return-based fee. A return-based fee is charged only on profits above a hurdle rate, subject to a high-water mark.

mocks.p: Which statement about “NAV” is correct?
o: NAV is the per-unit value of a scheme, equal to net assets divided by units outstanding.
PMS clients cannot see holdings.
NAV is used to value a PMS client's individual holdings.
An ETF is bought only from the AMC at NAV.
mocks.w: Correct: NAV is the per-unit value of a scheme, equal to net assets divided by units outstanding.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A return-based fee is charged only on profits above a hurdle rate, subject to a high-water mark.
A client cannot leave the PMS before 10 years.
Clients may contribute securities instead of cash, and the manager may hold them or realign the portfolio, with tax consequences.
The agreement between manager and client sets out services, fees, rights, risks, and termination terms, and is mandatory.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Either party may terminate the agreement as per its terms, usually with notice; assets are returned in the form specified.

mocks.p: A client uses the statement to compute her gains. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Turnover and tax
Dividend income
Capital gains statement
Set-off of losses
mocks.w: This is Capital gains statement. Managers provide a statement of realised gains and losses, which helps the client file her tax return.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A PMS portfolio is never reviewed once built.
Holding cash gives liquidity and flexibility but can drag returns in rising markets.
Portfolio turnover measures how much of the portfolio is bought and sold in a year; high turnover raises costs and taxes.
Position sizing sets how much of the portfolio is placed in each security, balancing conviction and risk.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The portfolio is reviewed regularly against objectives, benchmark and risk limits, and changes are made as needed.

mocks.p: A client owns part of a listed company. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Equity share
Growth investing
Return on equity
Price-to-book ratio
mocks.w: This is Equity share. An equity share represents ownership in a company with a residual claim on profits and assets.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A high down-capture ratio is desirable.
SEBI requires performance of portfolio managers to be reported in a uniform manner, using TWRR, through an independent central performance platform.
Evaluating a manager involves return, risk, consistency, process and costs, not just headline returns.
Style drift occurs when a manager moves away from the stated investment approach, which should be monitored.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Capture ratios show how much of the benchmark's up and down moves a portfolio captures; high up-capture and low down-capture is desirable.

mocks.p: A client must commit at least ₹50 lakh. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Advisory PMS
Minimum investment
Discretionary PMS
Registration of portfolio managers
mocks.w: This is Minimum investment. A client's minimum investment with a portfolio manager is ₹50 lakh, in funds or securities, with a lower threshold for accredited investors.

mocks.p: Buyers and sellers meet on an electronic platform. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: SEBI
Primary market
Stock exchange
Depository
mocks.w: This is Stock exchange. A stock exchange is a regulated platform where listed securities trade, such as the BSE and NSE.

mocks.p: A firm falls short on capital and cannot be registered. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Related-party dealing
Prohibition on assured returns
SEBI Portfolio Managers Regulations
Net worth requirement
mocks.w: This is Net worth requirement. A portfolio manager must maintain minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

mocks.p: A company with 10 crore shares at ₹300 is valued at ₹3,000 crore. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Equity risks
Market capitalisation
Sector concentration
Corporate governance
mocks.w: This is Market capitalisation. Market capitalisation is share price times shares outstanding, used to classify companies as large, mid or small cap.

mocks.p: A client receives a document describing the manager and charges before investing. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Client reporting
Portfolio management agreement
Audit and compliance
Disclosure document
mocks.w: This is Disclosure document. The disclosure document gives the client full information about the manager, investment approach, fees, risks and litigation before signing.

mocks.p: A manager charges 1% of assets plus 10% of profits above a hurdle. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Disclosure document
High-water mark
Exit load
Hybrid fee
mocks.w: This is Hybrid fee. A hybrid fee combines a lower fixed fee with a performance fee.

mocks.p: Each sale by the manager creates a tax event for the client. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Taxation at client level
Set-off of losses
Turnover and tax
Capital gains statement
mocks.w: This is Taxation at client level. PMS transactions are in the client's own name, so gains and losses are taxed directly in the client's hands.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Managers must avoid and disclose conflicts, such as trading in the same securities for own account ahead of clients.
Either party may terminate the agreement as per its terms, usually with notice; assets are returned in the form specified.
Clients may withdraw funds or securities as per the agreement, with notice and exit load as applicable.
Exit load is the same in every year.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Exit load is a charge on withdrawal in the early years: at most 3% in the first year, 2% in the second and 1% in the third, with none thereafter.

mocks.p: Two managers with equal returns are compared on risk taken. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Money-weighted return
Alpha
Up and down capture
Sharpe ratio
mocks.w: This is Sharpe ratio. The Sharpe ratio measures excess return per unit of total risk; a higher ratio means better risk-adjusted performance.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A high-water mark resets every month.
A fixed management fee is charged as a percentage of assets irrespective of performance.
A return-based fee is charged only on profits above a hurdle rate, subject to a high-water mark.
Managers must give clients periodic reports showing portfolio holdings, transactions, performance and charges.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The high-water mark is the highest value of the portfolio on which a performance fee was last paid; a new fee is charged only on gains above it.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Growth investing seeks companies with above-average earnings growth, often at higher valuations.
Large caps are generally more stable and liquid; small caps offer higher growth potential with more volatility and lower liquidity.
ROE is price divided by earnings.
P/B compares share price with book value per share, widely used for banks and asset-heavy companies.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: ROE is net profit divided by shareholders' equity and measures how effectively equity is used.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Distributors may guarantee returns.
A portfolio manager must maintain minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.
Managers must disclose and manage conflicts, avoid front running and not misuse client information.
Managers must disclose investments in related-party securities and avoid favouring group entities.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Portfolio managers and distributors cannot assure or guarantee returns on a PMS.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Investment objective” is correct?
o: Tactical allocation is a permanent allocation.
The investment objective is unrelated to the client's needs.
The investment objective states what the portfolio is meant to achieve, such as growth, income or capital preservation, with risk and time limits.
Rebalancing means adding to the best performers.
mocks.w: Correct: The investment objective states what the portfolio is meant to achieve, such as growth, income or capital preservation, with risk and time limits.

mocks.p: Equity drifts above target, so the manager trims it. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Rebalancing
Constraints
Cash in the portfolio
Passive management
mocks.w: This is Rebalancing. Rebalancing returns the portfolio to its target weights by selling what has risen and buying what has fallen.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Style drift” is correct?
o: Any index can serve as the benchmark.
Style drift occurs when a manager moves away from the stated investment approach, which should be monitored.
Standard deviation measures the average return.
Style drift is the sign of consistent discipline.
mocks.w: Correct: Style drift occurs when a manager moves away from the stated investment approach, which should be monitored.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Client assets must be kept separate from the manager's own assets, with a custodian required for safekeeping.
In advisory PMS the manager only advises; the client decides and executes.
Clients can invest in PMS only through distributors.
A portfolio manager cannot pool client funds the way a mutual fund does; each client's portfolio is managed individually.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Clients have the option to be onboarded directly with the portfolio manager without a distributor, and the manager must offer a direct plan.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Tactical allocation is a permanent allocation.
The portfolio is reviewed regularly against objectives, benchmark and risk limits, and changes are made as needed.
The investment objective states what the portfolio is meant to achieve, such as growth, income or capital preservation, with risk and time limits.
A concentrated portfolio holds few stocks, offering higher potential returns with higher risk.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Tactical allocation makes temporary deviations from the strategic weights to benefit from expected short-term moves.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Annualised return converts a return over any period into an equivalent yearly rate for comparison.
TWRR is affected by when the client adds money.
The money-weighted return (IRR) reflects the size and timing of cash flows and captures the client's actual experience.
Style drift occurs when a manager moves away from the stated investment approach, which should be monitored.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: TWRR removes the effect of cash inflows and outflows, so it measures the manager's skill independent of the client's timing.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Gains on listed shares held up to 12 months are short-term and over 12 months long-term, with different tax rates.
Fees are always deductible.
PMS transactions are in the client's own name, so gains and losses are taxed directly in the client's hands.
Capital losses can be set off against capital gains and carried forward as per the tax law.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Management fees and expenses may be deductible against gains or income as per the law, subject to conditions.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Compounding generates returns on past returns, growing wealth faster over long horizons.
Money received sooner is worth more than the same sum later because it can earn a return.
Inflation raises the real return of cash.
Investment risks include market, credit, liquidity, interest-rate and concentration risks.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money; real return is nominal return minus inflation, approximately.

mocks.p: A custodian holds the securities of PMS clients separately. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Advisory PMS
Discretionary PMS
Segregation of client assets
Distributor's role
mocks.w: This is Segregation of client assets. Client assets must be kept separate from the manager's own assets, with a custodian required for safekeeping.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Quality investing favours companies with high returns on capital, stable earnings and strong governance.
An equity share represents ownership in a company with a residual claim on profits and assets.
Dividends are guaranteed every year.
Large caps are generally more stable and liquid; small caps offer higher growth potential with more volatility and lower liquidity.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A dividend is a share of profit paid to shareholders, which forms part of total return along with price change.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Client assets must be kept separate from the manager's own assets, with a custodian required for safekeeping.
Clients have the option to be onboarded directly with the portfolio manager without a distributor, and the manager must offer a direct plan.
In discretionary PMS the client approves every trade.
Portfolio managers must provide an investor charter explaining the rights and obligations of clients and the grievance process.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: In discretionary PMS the manager takes investment decisions independently on behalf of the client, without asking approval for each trade.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The investment objective states what the portfolio is meant to achieve, such as growth, income or capital preservation, with risk and time limits.
Because each trade is taxed in the client's hands, managers consider holding period and tax impact when trading.
Passive managers pick stocks they expect to beat the market.
Constraints such as liquidity needs, time horizon, tax, legal limits and unique preferences shape what the portfolio can hold.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Passive management replicates an index at low cost, without attempting to outperform.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A manager needs only ₹10 lakh of net worth.
Managers must disclose and manage conflicts, avoid front running and not misuse client information.
Portfolio managers must not trade on unpublished price-sensitive information, and violations are prosecuted.
These regulations govern registration, conduct, fees, disclosures and client protection for portfolio managers.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A portfolio manager must maintain minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Derivative” is correct?
o: A derivative is a contract whose value depends on an underlying asset, such as a share or an index.
An option obliges the buyer to complete the trade.
Leverage reduces risk.
A derivative has no link to any underlying.
mocks.w: Correct: A derivative is a contract whose value depends on an underlying asset, such as a share or an index.

mocks.p: A client receives a document describing her rights. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Investor charter
Advisory PMS
Client's own account
Investment approach
mocks.w: This is Investor charter. Portfolio managers must provide an investor charter explaining the rights and obligations of clients and the grievance process.

mocks.p: A portfolio holds T-bills for liquidity. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Government security
Credit risk
Money market instruments
Credit rating
mocks.w: This is Money market instruments. Money market instruments mature within a year and are used to park short-term funds.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Annualised return converts a return over any period into an equivalent yearly rate for comparison.
Gross returns are before fees and expenses while net returns are after them; investors should compare net returns.
A benchmark is a standard index against which performance is compared, chosen to match the strategy.
Maximum drawdown measures the biggest gain.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Maximum drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough decline in portfolio value, showing worst-case loss experienced.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A bond is a debt instrument paying periodic interest (coupon) and repaying principal at maturity.
Money market instruments mature within a year and are used to park short-term funds.
Yield and price move in the same direction.
Credit risk is the possibility that the issuer fails to pay interest or principal on time.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The coupon is the fixed interest on face value, while yield is the return based on current price; yield rises when price falls.

mocks.p: An investor splits money between shares, bonds and gold. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Asset class
Compounding
Risk profile
Time value of money
mocks.w: This is Asset class. An asset class is a group of investments with similar characteristics, such as equity, fixed income, gold and real estate.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: SEBI regulates only banks.
A stock exchange is a regulated platform where listed securities trade, such as the BSE and NSE.
The secondary market is where existing securities trade between investors on exchanges, providing liquidity.
The primary market is where securities are first issued to investors and the issuer receives the proceeds.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: SEBI regulates the securities market including portfolio managers, and frames regulations to protect investors.

mocks.p: A PMS holds 15 stocks. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Cash in the portfolio
Concentrated portfolio
Active management
Suitability for PMS
mocks.w: This is Concentrated portfolio. A concentrated portfolio holds few stocks, offering higher potential returns with higher risk.

mocks.p: A manager buys shares based on confidential merger news. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Suitability by distributor
SEBI Portfolio Managers Regulations
Fiduciary duty
Insider trading
mocks.w: This is Insider trading. Portfolio managers must not trade on unpublished price-sensitive information, and violations are prosecuted.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Rebalancing returns the portfolio to its target weights by selling what has risen and buying what has fallen.
The investment objective states what the portfolio is meant to achieve, such as growth, income or capital preservation, with risk and time limits.
Turnover has no effect on costs.
Risk limits such as stop-losses, single-stock caps and sector caps control downside and discipline.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Portfolio turnover measures how much of the portfolio is bought and sold in a year; high turnover raises costs and taxes.

mocks.p: A bond bought below face value yields more than its coupon. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Credit risk
Duration
Credit rating
Coupon and yield
mocks.w: This is Coupon and yield. The coupon is the fixed interest on face value, while yield is the return based on current price; yield rises when price falls.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An ETF is a fund traded on exchanges, typically tracking an index at low cost.
NAV is the per-unit value of a scheme, equal to net assets divided by units outstanding.
A mutual fund pools money from many investors into a scheme managed by an AMC, with investors owning units.
PMS clients cannot see holdings.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: PMS clients see their own holdings and transactions, while mutual fund investors see a pooled portfolio.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Strategic allocation sets long-term target weights across asset classes, based on objectives and risk profile.
A concentrated portfolio holds few stocks, offering higher potential returns with higher risk.
Active managers track the index exactly.
Tactical allocation makes temporary deviations from the strategic weights to benefit from expected short-term moves.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Active management seeks to outperform a benchmark through selection and timing decisions, at higher cost.

mocks.p: A distributor refuses to oversell the product's features. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Insider trading
SEBI Portfolio Managers Regulations
Conflict of interest
Code of conduct for distributors
mocks.w: This is Code of conduct for distributors. Distributors must act honestly, avoid mis-selling, keep confidentiality and give true information about products.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Clients can complain to the manager, then to SEBI's complaint system, and use online dispute resolution.
Distributors must disclose commission earned from the portfolio manager to the client.
Managers must disclose and manage conflicts, avoid front running and not misuse client information.
Related-party holdings need not be disclosed.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Managers must disclose investments in related-party securities and avoid favouring group entities.

mocks.p: A client's shares are held electronically in a demat account. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: SEBI
Settlement
Stock exchange
Depository
mocks.w: This is Depository. A depository holds securities in electronic form, enabling transfer by book entry; India has NSDL and CDSL.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Money-weighted return ignores cash flow timing.
Evaluating a manager involves return, risk, consistency, process and costs, not just headline returns.
A benchmark is a standard index against which performance is compared, chosen to match the strategy.
SEBI requires performance of portfolio managers to be reported in a uniform manner, using TWRR, through an independent central performance platform.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The money-weighted return (IRR) reflects the size and timing of cash flows and captures the client's actual experience.

mocks.p: A PMS client checks each stock in her own portfolio. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Transparency
PMS versus mutual fund
NAV
Expense versus fee
mocks.w: This is Transparency. PMS clients see their own holdings and transactions, while mutual fund investors see a pooled portfolio.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A hurdle rate is the maximum fee permitted.
The disclosure document gives the client full information about the manager, investment approach, fees, risks and litigation before signing.
Clients may contribute securities instead of cash, and the manager may hold them or realign the portfolio, with tax consequences.
A custodian safekeeps the securities of PMS clients independent of the manager, and settles trades.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A hurdle rate is the minimum return the portfolio must earn before a performance fee is charged.

mocks.p: A portfolio's returns vary widely from month to month. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Standard deviation
Maximum drawdown
Time-weighted return
Benchmark
mocks.w: This is Standard deviation. Standard deviation measures the volatility of returns; higher values indicate more risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A stock exchange is a regulated platform where listed securities trade, such as the BSE and NSE.
A depository holds securities in electronic form, enabling transfer by book entry; India has NSDL and CDSL.
Investors trade with each other in the primary market.
Equity trades settle on T+1 through a clearing corporation, which guarantees settlement.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The primary market is where securities are first issued to investors and the issuer receives the proceeds.

mocks.p: A manager avoids a trade that benefits it at the client's expense. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Fiduciary duty
Conflict of interest
Insider trading
Commission disclosure
mocks.w: This is Fiduciary duty. The manager must act in the client's best interest, with care, diligence and loyalty, and place client interest before its own.

mocks.p: A manager's return is computed between each deposit or withdrawal and then chained. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Benchmark
Annualised return
Standard deviation
Time-weighted return
mocks.w: This is Time-weighted return. TWRR removes the effect of cash inflows and outflows, so it measures the manager's skill independent of the client's timing.

mocks.p: A small-cap stock falls sharply on a bad quarter. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Large, mid and small caps
Equity risks
Market capitalisation
Price-to-earnings ratio
mocks.w: This is Large, mid and small caps. Large caps are generally more stable and liquid; small caps offer higher growth potential with more volatility and lower liquidity.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Expense versus fee” is correct?
o: An AIF accepts small retail investments.
Mutual funds charge an expense ratio inside NAV, while PMS charges management and performance fees separately to the client.
An ETF is bought only from the AMC at NAV.
PMS has no fees.
mocks.w: Correct: Mutual funds charge an expense ratio inside NAV, while PMS charges management and performance fees separately to the client.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: P/B compares share price with book value per share, widely used for banks and asset-heavy companies.
P/E is the share price divided by earnings per share, showing how much investors pay per rupee of earnings.
Growth investors buy only stocks with the lowest P/E.
Large caps are generally more stable and liquid; small caps offer higher growth potential with more volatility and lower liquidity.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Growth investing seeks companies with above-average earnings growth, often at higher valuations.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: PMS pools all client money into one demat account.
Portfolio managers must provide an investor charter explaining the rights and obligations of clients and the grievance process.
Portfolio managers must be registered with SEBI and meet net-worth requirements; the minimum net worth is ₹5 crore.
An investment approach is a distinct style or strategy offered by a portfolio manager, such as large-cap growth or multi-cap value, with defined objectives and risks.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Securities in a PMS are held in a separate demat account in the client's name, giving ownership and transparency.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Cash in the portfolio” is correct?
o: Holding cash gives liquidity and flexibility but can drag returns in rising markets.
A PMS portfolio is never reviewed once built.
PMS suits investors needing money in a month.
Cash always improves returns.
mocks.w: Correct: Holding cash gives liquidity and flexibility but can drag returns in rising markets.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A depository holds securities in electronic form, enabling transfer by book entry; India has NSDL and CDSL.
A stock exchange is a regulated platform where listed securities trade, such as the BSE and NSE.
The primary market is where securities are first issued to investors and the issuer receives the proceeds.
Equity trades take a week to settle.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Equity trades settle on T+1 through a clearing corporation, which guarantees settlement.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Portfolio managers need no minimum net worth.
An investment approach is a distinct style or strategy offered by a portfolio manager, such as large-cap growth or multi-cap value, with defined objectives and risks.
In advisory PMS the manager only advises; the client decides and executes.
In discretionary PMS the manager takes investment decisions independently on behalf of the client, without asking approval for each trade.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Portfolio managers must be registered with SEBI and meet net-worth requirements; the minimum net worth is ₹5 crore.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The holding period for listed shares is 36 months.
Capital losses can be set off against capital gains and carried forward as per the tax law.
Dividend received on shares in the portfolio is taxable in the client's hands at the slab rate.
PMS transactions are in the client's own name, so gains and losses are taxed directly in the client's hands.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Gains on listed shares held up to 12 months are short-term and over 12 months long-term, with different tax rates.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Exit load” is correct?
o: Clients can contribute only cash.
Exit load is the same in every year.
Exit load is a charge on withdrawal in the early years: at most 3% in the first year, 2% in the second and 1% in the third, with none thereafter.
A PMS can start without a written agreement.
mocks.w: Correct: Exit load is a charge on withdrawal in the early years: at most 3% in the first year, 2% in the second and 1% in the third, with none thereafter.

mocks.p: A manager protects holdings with a put option. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Hedging
Leverage risk
Options
Futures
mocks.w: This is Hedging. Hedging uses derivatives to offset an existing risk, reducing the portfolio's exposure to adverse moves.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Value investing” is correct?
o: Value investors buy only the most expensive stocks.
Value investing buys stocks trading below estimated intrinsic value, expecting the price to converge.
P/B compares price with dividend.
Small caps are less volatile than large caps.
mocks.w: Correct: Value investing buys stocks trading below estimated intrinsic value, expecting the price to converge.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Penalties” is correct?
o: SEBI cannot act against portfolio managers.
SEBI can penalise, suspend or cancel registration of managers or distributors who violate the regulations.
Commissions are hidden from clients.
The manager may favour its own interest.
mocks.w: Correct: SEBI can penalise, suspend or cancel registration of managers or distributors who violate the regulations.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Clients may contribute securities instead of cash, and the manager may hold them or realign the portfolio, with tax consequences.
The agreement between manager and client sets out services, fees, rights, risks, and termination terms, and is mandatory.
Costs are not passed to PMS clients.
Clients may withdraw funds or securities as per the agreement, with notice and exit load as applicable.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Brokerage and other expenses on transactions, such as custodian and audit fees, are charged to the client as disclosed.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A credit rating is a guarantee of repayment.
A G-sec is issued by the government with negligible credit risk, though price changes with yields.
Duration measures a bond's price sensitivity to interest-rate changes; higher duration means larger price swings.
Money market instruments mature within a year and are used to park short-term funds.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A credit rating is an agency's opinion of an issuer's ability to repay, from AAA (highest) downward.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A derivative is a contract whose value depends on an underlying asset, such as a share or an index.
An option obliges the buyer to complete the trade.
Derivatives allow large exposure for small margin, magnifying gains and losses.
Hedging uses derivatives to offset an existing risk, reducing the portfolio's exposure to adverse moves.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: An option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell at a fixed price for a premium.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Investment risks include market, credit, liquidity, interest-rate and concentration risks.
A client's risk profile combines willingness and ability to bear loss and guides the portfolio mix.
Diversification spreads investments across securities and asset classes to reduce specific risk.
High return can be earned without any added risk.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Higher expected return generally requires acceptance of higher risk; investors are paid for bearing risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Diversification spreads investments across securities and asset classes to reduce specific risk.
Risk profile is irrelevant to PMS.
Higher expected return generally requires acceptance of higher risk; investors are paid for bearing risk.
An asset class is a group of investments with similar characteristics, such as equity, fixed income, gold and real estate.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A client's risk profile combines willingness and ability to bear loss and guides the portfolio mix.

mocks.p: A portfolio holding mostly banking stocks falls when banks fall. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Large, mid and small caps
Quality investing
Price-to-earnings ratio
Sector concentration
mocks.w: This is Sector concentration. Concentrating a portfolio in one sector raises risk because sector-specific shocks hit all holdings together.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Equity and debt are the same asset class.
Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money; real return is nominal return minus inflation, approximately.
Money received sooner is worth more than the same sum later because it can earn a return.
The investment horizon is the period for which funds can remain invested, affecting what assets are suitable.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: An asset class is a group of investments with similar characteristics, such as equity, fixed income, gold and real estate.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A futures contract is an exchange-traded agreement to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date.
An option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell at a fixed price for a premium.
Leverage reduces risk.
A derivative is a contract whose value depends on an underlying asset, such as a share or an index.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Derivatives allow large exposure for small margin, magnifying gains and losses.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The coupon is the fixed interest on face value, while yield is the return based on current price; yield rises when price falls.
A G-sec is issued by the government with negligible credit risk, though price changes with yields.
Duration is the bond's maturity date.
Credit risk is the possibility that the issuer fails to pay interest or principal on time.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Duration measures a bond's price sensitivity to interest-rate changes; higher duration means larger price swings.

mocks.p: A manager discloses related-party trades. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Hurdle rate
Withdrawals and partial redemptions
Conflict of interest
Client reporting
mocks.w: This is Conflict of interest. Managers must avoid and disclose conflicts, such as trading in the same securities for own account ahead of clients.

mocks.p: A registered firm invests a client's money under a signed agreement. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Segregation of client assets
Advisory PMS
Registration of portfolio managers
Portfolio manager
mocks.w: This is Portfolio manager. A portfolio manager is a SEBI-registered body corporate that manages or administers a client's securities or funds under a contract.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Diversification” is correct?
o: Diversification spreads investments across securities and asset classes to reduce specific risk.
Diversification removes all risk.
Risk profile is irrelevant to PMS.
High return can be earned without any added risk.
mocks.w: Correct: Diversification spreads investments across securities and asset classes to reduce specific risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Managers must avoid and disclose conflicts, such as trading in the same securities for own account ahead of clients.
The high-water mark is the highest value of the portfolio on which a performance fee was last paid; a new fee is charged only on gains above it.
A fixed fee depends on profits.
Either party may terminate the agreement as per its terms, usually with notice; assets are returned in the form specified.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A fixed management fee is charged as a percentage of assets irrespective of performance.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Client reporting” is correct?
o: The disclosure document is given after the first year.
Conflicts need not be disclosed.
Managers must give clients periodic reports showing portfolio holdings, transactions, performance and charges.
Managers need not report to clients.
mocks.w: Correct: Managers must give clients periodic reports showing portfolio holdings, transactions, performance and charges.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Portfolio managers must provide an investor charter explaining the rights and obligations of clients and the grievance process.
Client assets must be kept separate from the manager's own assets, with a custodian required for safekeeping.
In discretionary PMS the manager takes investment decisions independently on behalf of the client, without asking approval for each trade.
PMS invests all client money in a single pool.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A portfolio manager cannot pool client funds the way a mutual fund does; each client's portfolio is managed individually.

mocks.p: A manager offers a quality-focused multi-cap approach. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Distributor's role
Client's own account
Segregation of client assets
Investment approach
mocks.w: This is Investment approach. An investment approach is a distinct style or strategy offered by a portfolio manager, such as large-cap growth or multi-cap value, with defined objectives and risks.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The investment objective states what the portfolio is meant to achieve, such as growth, income or capital preservation, with risk and time limits.
Passive management replicates an index at low cost, without attempting to outperform.
An investment policy is a guarantee of returns.
Tactical allocation makes temporary deviations from the strategic weights to benefit from expected short-term moves.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The investment policy records objectives, constraints, allocation ranges and rebalancing rules, guiding the manager.

mocks.p: A manager avoids selling just before a gain becomes long-term. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Cash in the portfolio
Tax-aware management
Investment policy
Stop-loss and risk limits
mocks.w: This is Tax-aware management. Because each trade is taxed in the client's hands, managers consider holding period and tax impact when trading.

mocks.p: A manager avoids a company with weak disclosure. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Growth investing
Price-to-book ratio
